title: Verdigris ML pilot - budget & batching economics scoping
summary: AE + SE scoped a 6-week pilot to validate per-token economics, p95 latency targets and batching/caching knobs. Customer provided workload shape (avg 120 tokens, 10 reqs/sec peak) and a $5k/month budget cap for the initial pilot. Redwood proposed benchmarks (baseline hosted, dedicated small pool, and quantized variant) and set clear next steps: send cost model spreadsheet, schedule 2-hour benchmarking window, and align on success criteria (p95 < 650ms, inference cost < $0.0025 per token on pilot mix).
next_steps: Redwood to share pilot econ spreadsheet and example workload harness - due 2026-06-09
Schedule 2-hour benchmark run with Verdigris infra team - target week of 2026-06-15
Customer to provide 5k anonymized prompt samples and token distribution - due 2026-06-10
action_items: Arielle: Share cost model spreadsheet and example harness link; due 2026-06-09
Marco: Provide access details for benchmarking VPC (or provide representative sample logs); due 2026-06-10
Samir: Prepare dedicated config suggestions (pool sizes, batching knobs) and a runbook; due 2026-06-12
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-05 15:00 PT | Duration: 55m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Arielle, Samir (Redwood); Lena, Marco, Priya, Jonas (Verdigris)
---
[00:00] Arielle: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro - i'm Arielle, i'm the AE on the account, Samir's our SE. um, quick round-robin?
[00:10] Lena: lena here, head of ml at Verdigris. we're trying to get a pilot that proves out cost per inference for our summarization pipeline.
[00:18] Marco: Marco, infra. i'll run the bench env and coordinate VPC access.
[00:22] Priya: Priya, CTO. high level constraint: pilot budget is tight, so we need clear unit economics.
[00:27] Samir: great, thanks. can you describe the workload? traffic shape, average tokens, tail lengths?
[00:33] Jonas: sure, so typical prompt plus summary is about 120 tokens avg, responses maybe 250 tokens. peak concurrent ~10 reqs/sec during biz hours, avg 2-3. latency sensitivity is moderate — p95 target ideally under 500-700ms for our user flows.
[00:50] Arielle: useful — and what's the current stack? are you hitting OpenAI endpoints or running anything internally?
[00:56] Lena: currently hybrid: prototypes hitting OpenAI gpt-3.5 and a small in-house Llama 2 on a couple GPUs. cost is already painful on OpenAI for scale, and our infra team doesn't want to fully take on ops for long lived runtime. hence pilot to evaluate tradeoffs.
[01:12] Samir: okay, so main POI is per-token unit econ. quick framing: we run three bench lanes — hosted Redwood, a small dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) and a quantized model variant on same infra. we'll measure throughput, p95 latency, and tokens-per-second cost.
[01:28] Marco: what are the batching knobs? can batch size be tuned per route?
[01:32] Samir: yes, per-route batching. typical knobs: max batch size, batch delay (ms), and concurrency caps per GPU. also prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts — that can hugely reduce consumed tokens if you have a lot of shared context.
[01:46] Jonas: we do have a lot of shared templates, so KV cache could cut cost. but curious about cache warm-up and eviction behaviour.
[01:52] Samir: KV cache is maintained per-session and works at kv level; in practice for summarization it helps if you have large system instructions or long doc prefixes. warm-up depends on how many unique prefixes you have; we'll measure hit-rate during the bench. note: transcription may show KV cash in some docs ;)
[02:08] Lena: budget — the pilot has roughly a $5k monthly budget cap allocated. we need to know if we can run a 6-week pilot inside that.
[02:16] Arielle: good to know. our goal is to give you per-token estimates for your real mix: e.g. cost/token on hosted (no caching), cost/token with batching of 8 and batch delay 10ms, cost/token with caching hit rate 40%, and the quantized model variant. that will let us show you expected monthly burn for your projected QPS.
[02:36] Priya: do you have ballpark numbers today? even rough ranges help our finance folks.
[02:40] Samir: rough ballpark: for a 3.5B-ish open model on hosted, think $0.0018 - $0.003 per generated token depending on latency targets and batching. dedicated (reserved small pool) can bring that to $0.0009 - $0.0018 per token after amortized infra costs. quantized 4-bit/integer run could lower compute cost another ~20-40% but may impact quality. these are for illustration — we'll run your exact mix.
[03:05] Marco: okay interesting. do you show separate accounting for input tokens vs output tokens? audit line items?
[03:10] Arielle: yes, Redwood Console's cost breakdown has token-level lines and route-level attribution. we'll send a sample export.
[03:16] Jonas: on batching vs latency — sometimes users are impatient; we can't just arbitrarily increase batch delays. what's the expected p95 impact of batching of 8 with 10ms delay?
[03:25] Samir: depends on arrival distribution. with steady arrivals, batching of 8 at 10ms typically adds ~10-20ms extra queueing time but reduces per-token GPU overhead significantly, lowering unit cost. for bursty traffic it can increase p95 more; we can tune per-route and set SLOs with fallback to a low-latency pool.
[03:45] Lena: we care about regressions in quality — if we quantize, do you run evals?
[03:50] Samir: yes, Redwood Optimize might recommend quant profiles and we can run prompt-set evals during the pilot. we'll attach an eval harness and baseline metrics for Rouge/semantic similarity.
[03:59] Priya: security wise — we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), and audit logs for every inference. is that in scope for pilot?
[04:07] Arielle: SOC2 report is available; for pilot we can enable SSO + audit logging in the private plane or dedicated environment. we'll share the security pack.
[04:16] Marco: for benchmarks, do you prefer us to open a VPC peering or share sample logs?
[04:21] Samir: either works. peering is ideal for the dedicated lane; for hosted bench you can just run the harness hitting hosted endpoints. we'll outline both options.
[04:30] Jonas: can you put together a small spreadsheet that shows breakouts: tokens/day, tokens/month, cost/token for each lane, and expected monthly spend at our traffic?
[04:37] Arielle: yes — that's the cost model spreadsheet we'll send. it will include sensitivity sliders for batching, cache hit-rate, and quantization.
[04:44] Lena: success criteria — let's draft one now: (1) p95 latency <= 650ms for pilot request mix; (2) end-to-end inferred cost <= $0.0025 per token on pilot mix OR total pilot spend <= $5k/month; (3) no material quality regression (delta Rouge < 0.02) for quantized variant. agree?
[05:03] Priya: yep, that sounds reasonable.
[05:05] Samir: we'll aim to validate all three. for p95 we'll capture CPU/GPU metrics and Console traces.
[05:13] Arielle: timeline proposal: week 1 — share spreadsheet and harness; week 2 — customer provides samples and infra access; weeks 3-4 — run bench lanes and gather metrics; week 5 — quality evals and review; week 6 — final econ write-up and recommendation. total ~6 weeks.
[05:29] Marco: that timeline works for infra. small ask — can we run a short dry-run to validate our harness before the main bench?
[05:35] Samir: absolutely — we'll schedule a 2-hour dry-run session first.
[05:38] Jonas: about caching — what kind of hit-rates do you expect for repeated system prompts? we may get 30-60% depending on user behavior.
[05:45] Samir: if templates are consistent, 40% hit-rate is reasonable; we'll measure and show delta. remember caching mainly saves COMPUTE, not necessarily output tokens if you still generate same response length.
[05:57] Lena: billing question — if we run dedicated reserved capacity for pilot, is there a minimum commit?
[05:61] Arielle: for short pilots we can do an experimental reserved pool with a short-term commit (monthly pro-rate), or run on dedicated burst mode. we'll detail options in the spreadsheet.
[06:12] Priya: do you have any reference customers with similar summarization workloads?
[06:16] Arielle: yes — we'll anonymize two case studies: one saw ~30% token cost reduction after batching+cache; another adopted a quantized variant but needed slight prompt tuning to retain quality.
[06:26] Marco: one more on telemetry — we need per-token traces to attribute cost to product routes. can Redwood surface that?
[06:31] Samir: yes, Console has route-level token breakdown, trace IDs, and latency histograms. we'll show a sample export.
[06:38] Lena: ok, let's capture next steps.
[06:41] Arielle: recap: send cost model + harness by Tues 6/9, customer to give sample prompts and infra details by 6/10, schedule 2-hour dry-run week of 6/15, full bench after dry-run, final write-up end of June.
[06:55] Priya: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[06:58] Jonas: thanks.
[07:00] Arielle: i'll follow up with the calendar invites and links to the spreadsheet + security pack. bye.

End transcript.
